components.basis: Definition (body 15-35): real integrable family on (Omega,F,P); uniform integrability as lim_M sup_i E(|X_i| 1{|X_i|>M}) = 0; empty-family convention (boundary); uniform small-event control; notation E(Z;A); versions without completeness. Source variant (Durrett p. 244: any collection, no integrability assumed; the remark sup_i E|X_i| <= M+1 < infinity that 'will be useful several times') is preserved on the route at w02c-p15-014 body 554-597 (Durrett's form, integrability derived, infinite-mean member excluded, equivalence of the two definitions) with written proof at its annex 466-503.

Statement (body 37-46): UI iff L1-bounded plus uniform small-event control; integrable domination; finite families; bounded first moments insufficient. Annex 3-32 writes every direction: empty family; M+1 bound; E(|X_i|;A) <= M P(A) + tail with delta = eps/(2M); converse by Markov with the C=0 case; domination via E(Z;Z>M) -> 0; finite family via Z = sum |X_i|; counterexample n 1_(0,1/n) (boundary). Durrett's 'trivial example' of domination (p. 244) preserved.

Statement (body 48-61): Borel superlinear Phi with sup_i E Phi(|X_i|) < infinity gives UI; Durrett's examples t^p (p>1) and t log+ t; explicit continuous convex nondecreasing converse with Phi(0)=0 and sup_i E Phi <= 1. Annex 34-74: tail bound from t <= eps Phi(t), C=0 case, recursive a_j, Phi = sum (t - a_j)^+ finite/continuous/convex/superlinear, E Phi <= 1 by monotone convergence, empty family. Durrett Thm 4.6.2 variant (p. 245: any phi >= 0, no integrability, eps_M = sup{x/phi(x): x >= M}, offered as 'a common way to check') preserved at w02c-p15-014 body 599-634 with proof at its annex 505-549; worked example 636-649 and limits 651-672 (boundary).

Statement (body 63-72) = Durrett Thm 4.6.1 (p. 244): {E(X|G): G any sub-sigma-algebra} is UI, with no nesting or countability assumption (the source's point that UI families 'can be very large'). Annex 76-99: delta for the singleton from the tail-splitting proof, V_G = E(|X| | G), Markov P(V_G > M) <= delta, conditional Jensen, defining identity on {V_G > M}, one M for every G, boundary E|X| = 0. Durrett's chain of inequalities is written; the delta step is proved by a different written route, not by citation.

Statement (body 77-93): L1 implies probability; a.s. subsequence; bounded convergence in probability; Fatou in probability with infinite expectations allowed; event integrals converge uniformly in A (Durrett Lemma 4.6.5, p. 246, strengthened to uniformity). Annex 101-134 proves all five (Markov; Borel-Cantelli subsequence; eps + 2K P(.) bound with K=0 case; Fatou along an a.s. subsequence incl. infinite and zero lower limits; event bound). Supplies the Chapter 2 tools Durrett invokes in Thm 4.6.3 (Lemma 2.2.2, Exs. 2.3.4-2.3.5).

Statement (body 95-108) = Durrett Thm 4.6.3 (p. 245): E|X_n| < infinity, X_n -> X in probability; (i) UI, (ii) L1 convergence, (iii) E|X_n| -> E|X| < infinity equivalent; both source truncations named. Annex 136-197: (i)=>(ii) with the clipping phi_M, E|X| < infinity by Fatou in probability, three-term pointwise bound, limsup <= 2 eps; (ii)=>(iii) by |E|X_n| - E|X|| <= E|X_n - X|; (iii)=>(i) with Durrett's piecewise-linear psi_M, n_0, and the threshold increase for n < n_0 shown not to disturb n >= n_0. Boundary examples for the hypotheses at thm:p15-ui-counterexamples (1)-(2).

Statement (body 110-121) = Durrett Thm 4.6.4 (p. 246): for a submartingale UI, a.s.+L1 convergence and L1 convergence are equivalent; plus supermartingale sign change, F_infinity-measurable limit and X_n <= E(X_infinity | F_n). Annex 199-224: L1 bound gives the positive-part bound, a.s. limit from the proved convergence theorem (martingales-and-convergence 198-214), measurable version, Vitali both ways, conditional inequality via event integrals, the L1 limit and a 1/k contradiction, supermartingale via -X.

Definition (body 123-130): martingale closed by Z in L1, F_infinity = sigma(union F_n); boundary remark that Z need not be F_infinity-measurable. Matches Durrett Thm 4.6.7 (iv) (p. 247): an integrable X with X_n = E(X | F_n).

Statement (body 132-143) = Durrett Thm 4.6.7 (p. 247) four equivalences with Lemma 4.6.6 (p. 246) X_n = E(X_infinity | F_n), plus X_infinity = E(Z | F_infinity) for every closing Z. Annex 226-258: first three by the submartingale result; (iii)=>(iv) by event integrals passed to the L1 limit (Lemmas 4.6.5-4.6.6 argument); (iv)=>(i) by the conditional-family theorem; identification by a written lambda-system/pi-system argument with dominated convergence on disjoint unions.

Statement (body 148-159) = Durrett Thm 4.6.8 (p. 247): E(Z | F_n) -> E(Z | F_infinity) a.s. and in L1, limit defined measurably on the exceptional set. Annex 260-285: martingale by the tower identity, UI by the conditional-family theorem, convergence by the closed-martingale theorem, F_infinity-measurable version, event identity passed to the L1 limit, pi-lambda identification; no completeness assumed. Durrett's proof steps written out.

Statement (body 161-176) = Durrett Thm 4.6.9, Levy's 0-1 law (p. 247; the name is indexed and used at w02c-p15-014 680), with L1 added, and the tail zero-one law as its consequence. Annex 287-305: E(1_A | F_infinity) = 1_A and the upward theorem; tail event independent of F_n, E(1_A | F_n) = P(A), one null set, P(A) in {0,1}. Durrett's continuation (Chung's line 'obvious or incredible', the obvious and incredible readings, the evaluation 'very useful', pp. 247-248) preserved at w02c-p15-014 body 677-722.

Statement (body 178-195) = Durrett Ex. 4.6.7 (item 1) and Thm 4.6.10 (item 2, with L1 added), |Y| <= Z remark, oscillation envelopes W_N. Annex 307-349: L1 contraction plus the upward theorem; dominated convergence for the L1 part; W_N measurable, <= 2Z, decreasing to 0; conditional order and the upward theorem for each N on one null set; conditional dominated convergence; conditional Jensen; upward theorem for Y; triangle inequality (Durrett's p. 248 proof written out). Source title 'dominated convergence theorem for conditional expectations', its relation to the fixed-information case and the failure without domination preserved at w02c-p15-014 body 749-775.

Statement (body 197-218): three limits incl. Durrett Example 4.6.11 (p. 248) as B_n, C_n with X_n = n B_n C_n (Durrett's Y_n and Z_n = n C_n). Annex 351-390 proves each: a.s. to 0, mean 1, not UI; UI with |X_n| = 1 and no limit in probability; product-space construction, P(X_n > 0) = 1/n^2, first Borel-Cantelli, explicit tails, UI, E(X_n | G) = B_n by independence, second Borel-Cantelli for ones and zeros, L1 but not a.s. Durrett's preface (UI + a.s. gives conditional L1 convergence via Thm 4.6.3 and Ex. 4.6.7) is carried by thm:p15-vitali-convergence, thm:p15-changing-conditional-limits (1) and w02c-p15-014 770-773.

Definition (body 220-227) = Durrett's setting for Exs. 4.6.2-4.6.3 (p. 249): Omega = [0,1), I_{k,n}, D_n = sigma(I_{k,n}: 0 <= k < 2^n), uniform probability; boundary: atom mass 2^{-n}, right endpoint may equal one.

Statement (body 229-254) = Durrett Exs. 4.6.2-4.6.3 (p. 249): cell-average formula, a.e. and L1 convergence, step-function approximation, completed-Lebesgue extension; Lipschitz definition (Durrett's bold term), slopes as a bounded martingale with a.e./L1 limit, f(b) - f(a) = integral of X_infinity, continuous extension to the endpoint 1 that Durrett's formula needs. Annex 392-456 proves generation of the Borel sets by dyadic atoms, the conditional formula, the completion reduction, the extension to 1, the martingale identity, |X_infinity| <= K, the telescoping identity at dyadic endpoints and the passage to all endpoints incl. a = b. Durrett's remark comparing with Ex. 1.4.3 ('much simpler', 'a lot of machinery') preserved at w02c-p15-014 body 724-747.

Statement (body 256-270) = Durrett Ex. 4.6.1 (p. 248): i.i.d. integrable noise, independent integrable theta, Y_i = theta + xi_i, E(theta | F_n) -> theta a.s. (and in L1), the normal(0,1) case, scope qualification (boundary). Annex 458-479: strong law, F_infinity-measurable version L - mu of theta, upward theorem; no prior density or conjugacy. Durrett's statistical reading (normal population, variance 1, unknown mean) and his terms prior distribution and posterior distribution preserved at w02c-p15-014 body 777-826, with the posterior-mean corollary proved at its annex 554-589.

Statement (body 272-295) = Durrett Exs. 4.6.4-4.6.5 (p. 249): D = union {X_n = 0}, delta_K bound on {X_n <= K} (equivalent to Durrett's delta(x) for real x, since {X_n <= x} is contained in {X_n <= max(1, ceil(x))} for x >= 0 and is empty for x < 0), P(D union {X_n -> infinity}) = 1; branching process with p_0 > 0, an a.s. finite random start generalizing a fixed one, no mean assumption, empty sum. Annex 481-515: Levy's event theorem on one null set and the delta_K contradiction; generation filtration, P(Z_{n+1} = 0 | H_n) = p_0^{Z_n} incl. m = 0, transfer to the natural filtration, shifted sequence, absorption at 0.

Statement (body 297-310) = Durrett Ex. 4.6.6 (p. 249): alpha, beta in (0,1) with alpha + beta = 1 (equivalent to Durrett's alpha, beta > 0), X_n in [0,1] adapted with the two conditional probabilities; a.s. and L1 limit in {0,1}, P(X_infinity = 1) = E X_0, deterministic X_0 = theta gives theta. Annex 517-547: exhaustion of the conditional law, martingale identity, bounded hence UI, limit of X_{n+1} - beta X_n in {0, alpha} on one null set, alpha X_infinity in {0, alpha}; realizability construction incl. X_n = 0, 1 (boundary).

Definition (body 315-330): decreasing G_n, E(Y_n | G_{n+1}) = Y_{n+1}, tower consequence, G_infinity = intersection, and Durrett's negative-index convention X_{-n} = Y_n, F_{-n} = G_n with E(X_{k+1} | F_k) = X_k for k <= -1 (p. 249). Durrett's term 'backwards', the alternative name 'reversed' and his justificatory claim that decreasing sigma-fields make the convergence theory simple are preserved with the reason at w02c-p15-014 body 828-876.

Statement (body 332-342) = Durrett Thms 4.7.1-4.7.2 (pp. 249-250): UI, real G_infinity-measurable a.s. and L1 limit, Y_infinity = E(Y_0 | G_infinity), finite-string upcrossing method. Annex 549-614: Y_n = E(Y_0 | G_n) by induction, UI and the L1 bound; each reversed finite string as a forward martingale; the proved upcrossing inequality (martingales-and-convergence 184-196, greedy count maximal) gives (b-a) E U_n <= E(Y_0 - a)^+; monotonicity in n and monotone convergence; rational-pair argument for the extended limit; Fatou for finiteness; G_infinity-measurable version without completeness; Vitali for L1; identification by event integrals (Durrett's 4.7.2 proof).

Statement (body 344-355) = Durrett Thm 4.7.3 (p. 250, 'Theorem 4.6.8 backwards'): E(Z | G_n) -> E(Z | G_infinity) a.s. and in L1, plus a coordinatewise finite-dimensional extension. Annex 616-643: Y_n = E(Z | G_n) is a backward martingale by the tower identity, its limit E(Y_0 | G_infinity) = E(Z | G_infinity) by the tower identity with G_infinity in G_0; the vector extension with one null set and norm comparison written.

defect_observations: Attribution placement (not a coverage gap under the chapter's uniform end-of-entry citation convention): the closing \cite of thm:p15-levy-backward (body 351-354) follows the handbook's finite-dimensional vector extension, which Durrett Thm 4.7.3 does not contain; likewise the closing cites of thm:p15-posterior-mean-consistency (267-269) and thm:p15-extinction-or-escape (293-294) follow handbook-added qualifications. A sentence-level reader could take these as source claims; a short 'the extension is added here' clause would remove the ambiguity.

thm:p15-closed-martingale (body 140-142) attaches [lems 4.6.5-6, thm 4.6.7] to the identification X_infinity = E(Z | F_infinity) for a general closing Z; that identification is the argument of Durrett's Thm 4.6.8 proof (p. 247), which C010 cites. Content is sourced; the locator is imprecise.

Terse elementary steps (judged written, not missing): the pointwise bound |x - phi_M(x)| <= |x| 1{|x|>M} behind annex 146-153 is used without Durrett's one-line identity (|x| - M)^+; the remark |Y| <= Z a.s. (body 188) is not separately derived (limit of |Y_n| <= Z).
